pr_title: CSS:Tests: Fix tests & support tests under CSS Zoom
pr_body:
### Summary ###
<!--
Describe what this PR does. All but trivial changes (e.g. typos)
should start with an issue. Mention the issue number here.
-->

Firefox 126+ implements CSS zoom in a way it affects width computed style
very slightly (`100.008px` instead of `100px`); accept that difference.

Add a test for support tests resolving the same under CSS zoom & without one.
That test uncovered Chrome failing the `reliableTrDimensions` support test
under zoom; the test has been fixed.

Fixes gh-5489
Closes gh-5495
Ref gh-5496

`3.x` version: gh-5496

issue_context.title: Fix CSS test issues in Firefox coming from CSS zoom support
issue_context.body: ### Description ### Firefox implemented CSS zoom in version 126. That version fails our CSS tests. Snapshot from `main`: Snapshot from `3.x-stable`: The `main` version may just need a test tweak but the `3.x-stable` one seems like a genuine failure. We'll need to investigate before the next release. ### Link to test case ### N/A, our own tests are failing.
comments:
It looks like in Firefox 126 stable zoom affects `offsetWidth` values. In 127 Developer Edition & 128 Nightly it does not, just like it does not in Chrome.

Fortunately, [Firefox 126 will not be ESR](https://whattrainisitnow.com/calendar/).
I'd like to fix this before beta.2, even if just a test fix.

review_comments: IE / Edge, for which this support test was written, have much bigger differences here (something like 3 vs. 9) so rounding shouldn't affect it.
